a7155.speech: “CPHIA is a vital part of ongoing efforts by African countries and Africa CDC to build stronger, self-reliant health systems” ; “It provides an important platform for leaders, public health experts, and communities to come together to reimagine and transform health financing, ensuring Africa’s health security is driven by African leadership, innovation and partnerships.”

a7155.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a7155.speech: According to the report, this year’s conference also holds strategic global significance: it will precede the G20 Health Ministers’ meeting taking place under South Africa’s Presidency in early November 2025, and the CPHIA 2025 Outcome Declaration – the “Durban Declaration” – will capture Africa’s collective voice, positioning African-led solutions at the centre of global health reform.

a7155.speaker: Professor Olive Shisana, CPHIA 2025 Co-Chair (President, Evidence Based Solutions)
a7155.speech: “CPHIA is a critical opportunity to promote an African-led agenda for health, anchored in self-reliance and transformation.” ; “We aim to align around a Durban Declaration that ensures these priorities are front and centre during the G20 and Global Fund Meetings in November.”

a7155.speaker: Dr. Nhlanhla Msomi, President of AfricaBio
a7155.speech: “The BIO Africa Convention is proud to join forces with Africa CDC to connect science, innovation, and enterprise with public health,” ; “Together, we can harness the continent’s life sciences ecosystem to drive health resilience and self-reliance.”

a7308.speaker: Edoardo Campanella, senior fellow at the Mossavar-Rahmani Center for Business & Government, Harvard Kennedy School
a7308.speech: Warns that self-reliance strategies tend to lead to systemic instability and fuel international tensions - or worse; argues that to prevent the global economy's costly fragmentation into separate blocs, we need less authoritarian-versus-democratic rhetoric, greater efforts to separate economic issues from concerns about values, and a renewed diplomatic focus on the global commons, and that mutual reliance among countries should be the goal.

a7308.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a7308.speech: In his 2022 State of the Union address, promised to create an economy where "everything from the deck of an aircraft carrier to the steel on highway guardrails is made in America from beginning to end. All of it."

a7308.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a7308.speech: Declared early in his presidency that "America is back."

a7308.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a7308.speech: Has proposed that the European Union (EU) pursue its own "Made in Europe" strategy.

a7308.speaker: Narendra Modi, Indian Prime Minister
a7308.speech: Has also vowed to create a "self-reliant India."

a7308.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a7308.speech: Revived in 2018 Mao Zedong's slogan of "regeneration through one's efforts."

a7308.speaker: Leading intellectual exponents of self-sufficiency (Englebert Kaempfer, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Johann Fichte, Mohandas Gandhi, John Maynard Keynes)
a7308.speech: Mistakenly assumed that such strategies contributed to international peace by insulating countries from foreign influences that encouraged war.

a7312.speaker: Save the Children
a7312.speech: Announced a new Grants-under-Grant program in which the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Growth Through Nutrition Project will provide more than nine million Ethiopian birr (more than USD 300,000) to three woredas in support of the Government of Ethiopia's Seqota Declaration to end child under-nutrition by 2030; over the next year, the grants will support Debark and Ebinat woredas in Amhara regional state, and Nader Adet woreda in Tigray, by strengthening the woreda authorities' capacity to deliver locally appropriate nutrition interventions.

a7480.speaker: Tione Chilambe, National Aids Commission (NAC) head of coordination and capacity building
a7480.speech: Says Malawi expected donor support to decline over time, but not as quickly as it has happened following the shutdown of US Agency for International Development (USAid). “We knew the money would reduce, but not in such a painful and quick way,” she tells The Nation.

a7480.speaker: Tione Chilambe, National Aids Commission (NAC) head of coordination and capacity building
a7480.speech: Said the government responded by allocating $600 000 (about K1.1 billion) towards HIV treatment and an additional $1.4 million (K2.5 billion) for transporting lab samples used in testing ; “These efforts have helped stabilise services across the country.”

a7480.speaker: Ministry of Health (internal review)
a7480.speech: Shows that over half of HIV services in Malawi are funded by donors. The hugely donor-dependent services include HIV treatment, staffing and data systems.

a7480.speaker: Health experts in Malawi
a7480.speech: Fear that progress towards the UNAids 95-95-95 targets could be reversed, slowing the global push to end Aids-related deaths.

a7480.speaker: Experts at the Kigali meeting (International Aids Society Conference on HIV Science)
a7480.speech: Said countries must find new ways to raise money locally.

a7480.speaker: UNAids
a7480.speech: Has warned that if the funding gap is not filled, there could be an additional six million HIV infections and four million Aids-related deaths globally by 2029.

a7480.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAids executive director
a7480.speech: “We cannot let funding cuts wipe out the gains we’ve made. This is a moment for countries to step up, own their responses and invest in the health of their people.”

a7480.speaker: Musa Manganye, head of HIV treatment in South Africa
a7480.speech: Added that real commitment must go beyond speeches. “What matters is the budget line. That’s what shows real commitment.”
